_: THE DISCRETE SPAN VOCABULARY — A PROPOSAL, awaiting the maintainer. Nothing here is wired into docs/atlas/composition/src yet; 24667ce remains the checkpoint.
theProblem: The catalogue has patterns, but the slots inside them are still continuous: a subdesign writes its own grid-areas rows by hand, so a region can be any width and the columns beside it can belong to nobody. That is how `paired` came to leave 474px of unowned page, and how a 3:4 photograph came to be painted 1152x1536 — both technically valid, both obviously wrong.
theFix: A ROW IS A NAMED SPLIT, AND AREAS ARE GENERATED FROM IT. A subdesign no longer writes column strings; it names a split from this vocabulary and says which region holds which slot. Every column of every row then belongs to something by construction, and a footprint that is not in this table cannot be expressed at all.
notAResolver: None of this measures anything. A split is chosen from the surface and the media's geometry class — both categorical — and the set of splits a pattern may use is authored, not computed. The program is not deciding whether a page looks balanced; it is choosing among a handful of arrangements a human already decided are balanced.

regionRoles._: What a region of a split may be. There is no fourth option, which is what makes an unnamed column impossible rather than merely discouraged.
regionRoles.slot: a named slot of the pattern.
regionRoles.reading-margin: free columns BESIDE A PROSE SLOT, because prose is bound by the reading measure and the page is wider. Legal only in a split whose other region holds prose.
regionRoles.containment: the free columns either side of a CENTRED split. The split declares them, so they are part of the composition. Legal only in a centred split, and always symmetric.

4/8.note: a narrow leading region and a dominant one

5/7.note: the shape practice.workbook already uses: a reference column beside a workspace

6/6.note: TWO EQUAL CASES. Identical width IS the argument; this is the only split where equality is the point

8/4.note: a dominant leading region and a narrow one

tablet._: SEPARATELY APPROVED, not the desktop design squeezed. Eight columns is a different vocabulary, and a control refuses a tablet row whose split is merely the desktop split scaled.

7/1.note: THE TABLET PROSE ROW. Seven columns is 727px, the most this surface can give prose without passing the 760px measure; the eighth is its reading margin. `full-8` is 834px and may hold media, never prose.

phone._: At 382px there is no pairing to keep and no containment worth declaring. One split, and everything stacks.

pairingRule._: WHEN A `pair` SPLIT IS LEGITIMATE. Re-derived from the measurements in the slot-fit atlas, which put numbers on what the earlier rule had only asserted.
pairingRule.rule: A pair split is legitimate when BOTH regions have a height the author did not write: two cases of the same kind at identical width, or a region whose height is designed (a workspace's paper, an instrument's frame) beside one that is not.
pairingRule.forbidden: AN OBJECT BESIDE PROSE. The object's height is derived and the prose's is written, so the gap between them is a property of the sentence the author happened to type. Measured on identical filler: visual.explanation/side-6 left +474px and interactive.primary/beside +472px. practice.workbook/beside is sound at +139px to -263px, because its neighbour is a workspace with a designed height.
pairingRule.consequence: `visual.explanation` and `interactive.primary` stop pairing and become CENTRED SPINES. `visual.compare` keeps 6/6, because two equal cases is exactly what that split is for. `practice.workbook` keeps 5/7.
